findings.reason: The protected query cleanly separates company-level bracket selection from employee-level salary calculation. The company_rates CTE, take_home_percent name, three ordered CASE branches, equality join, and final ROUND expression are concise and conventional, with no unnecessary window, correlation, or repeated aggregation. No material improvement warrants an inert candidate.

Grouping by company_id computes the maximum over exactly that company's employees and maps it to one of the disjoint 100%, 76%, or 51% take-home rates. The join attaches that single company rate to every employee in the same company, and multiplying before ROUND applies the tax once to the final salary. Because the first condition is strict and the second inclusive, maxima of exactly 1000 and 10000 enter the 24% bracket, while 10001 enters the 49% bracket.

Under the declared hash-aggregation and hash-join model, one scan of E employees builds C company maxima and a second linear pass joins those aggregates back to the employees, giving O(E + C) expected time and O(C) auxiliary state. The complexity artifact is inherited, hash-bound identity only; this accelerated review did not inspect or recalibrate it and did not claim a fresh runtime verdict.

The query preserves the composite employee identity, company and employee names, company-wide maximum rule, exact 0%, 24%, and 49% boundaries, nearest-integer rounding, and unrestricted output order. A low-paid employee correctly receives the bracket selected by a higher-paid colleague rather than a rate selected from the employee's own salary.

The complete Approach accurately derives company-level aggregation, joining the chosen take-home percentage back to each employee, final-value rounding, and every threshold boundary. Its O(E + C) and O(C) claims match the protected query and variant manifest, and its alternatives and edge cases cover a window maximum, correlated and pairwise scans, both exact thresholds, cross-employee bracket effects, rounding, one-employee companies, and unordered results.

The protected app-local and immutable native SQL files are byte-identical and remain unchanged at canonical SHA-256 5f8df19954633e7a985f046f31e360b6d5fe9f7f3e1de1f5e5e6b4abac56cbea. They use the same aggregate, CASE thresholds, join, projection, and rounding expression, while verified submission 2074749008 remains untouched.

Authenticated Premium evidence confirmed the four-column Salaries schema and composite key, nearest-integer rounding, three company-maximum tax brackets, unrestricted row order, and one ten-row explained example. The modular Reference preserves all input and output rows, all three company maxima and rates, the after-tax formula, and the complete Morninngcat calculation, with no invented examples or ancillary sections. It is bound to live content SHA-256 f664f3fcf4447d4c2472c9e017471858bb4799b05c7420a91fd1e917f71df270.
